# Intermountain Health Logan Regional Hospital Unveils Gossner Cancer Center Radiation Oncology Expansion, Bringing Advanced Cancer Care to Northern Utah

Ribbon 1

Intermountain Health Logan Regional Hospital celebrated the opening of the Gossner Cancer Center Radiation Oncology expansion today, marking a significant investment in advanced cancer care for patients across Northern Utah and surrounding communities.

The expansion strengthens access to specialized cancer treatment and brings leading-edge technology and enhanced care capabilities closer to home for patients in Northern Utah.

The newly expanded facility includes a High Dose Rate (HDR) Brachytherapy Suite, GE Widebore CT Simulator, Varian TrueBeam Linear Accelerator Vault and control room, patient recovery and holding room, and a Radioligand Hot Lab and procedure suite.

Together, these additions significantly enhance Intermountain Logan Regional Hospital’s ability to provide comprehensive, precision-focused cancer care while improving the overall patient experience.

# New Cancer Campus Begins to Rise in Vineyard

Sep 02, 2026

Read Time: 7 minutes

### Takeaways:

  * Construction is moving from groundwork to visible vertical progress, with extensive site preparation complete and 830 deep foundation supports installed. 
  * The Vineyard campus will bring more access to world-class cancer care, research, education, and innovation closer to Utah County families and communities across the Mountain West—a region that is one of the fastest-growing in the country and includes vast areas of rural and frontier communities. 

Impact: In 2025 alone, Huntsman Cancer Institute hosted more than 52,000 patient visits from Utah County and adjacent areas, with patients traveling approximately 3.9 million miles to access care in Salt Lake City. The Vineyard campus is designed to bring comprehensive cancer expertise closer to communities we serve, reducing travel burdens while expanding access to care, research, student training, and support. 

Huntsman Cancer Institute at the University of Utah celebrated a major milestone Tuesday in the development of Huntsman Cancer Institute in Vineyard, gathering community leaders, elected officials, donors, supporters, and residents for a cornerstone celebration marking the start of vertical construction on the future cancer campus. The event celebrated Huntsman Cancer Institute's long-term commitment to Vineyard, Utah County, and the families who will benefit from expanded access to cancer care, research, education, and innovation throughout the region. 

Since the groundbreaking in April 2025, months of planning, design, engineering, and site preparation have transformed the future campus from a concept into a visible presence within the community. Crews have prepared the site, removed groundwater to enable excavation, and installed 830 deep foundation supports that will help anchor the building for decades to come. 

Now, the project enters an exciting new chapter as foundation work continues and vertical construction begins. The milestone marks the transition from site preparation to the visible rise of a new cancer care and research facility that will bring lifesaving services closer to patients, expand research and innovation, and strengthen access to comprehensive cancer expertise for communities throughout Utah and the Mountain West.

Left to right: Mike Frye, Darla Lambson and Alexis Kaufusi at the Vineyard Cornerstone Event. The mile marker signs featured throughout this story represent the distance many Utah County patients have traveled to receive care at Huntsman Cancer Institute. Their stories illustrate why bringing cancer care, research, and support services closer to home through our future Vineyard location matters so deeply to patients and families.

The need remains clear: In 2025 alone, Huntsman Cancer Institute hosted more than 52,000 patient visits from Utah County and adjacent areas, with patients traveling approximately 3.9 million miles—the equivalent of 86,000 hours of travel time. The Vineyard location will ease the travel burden for patients in central and southern portions of the state and beyond, saving patients more than two hours of travel time per visit, or an estimated 1.1 million miles per year.  
"Huntsman Cancer Institute in Vineyard is about much more than a new building," says Bradley Cairns, PhD, chief executive officer of Huntsman Cancer Institute. "It’s a deliberate commitment to grow with Utah County by becoming a steady, trusted presence in this community. We are listening, learning, and working alongside local leaders, health partners, educators, businesses, donors, and families to expand access to cancer prevention, screening, treatment, innovation and hope. At the center of that work are our patients. Their courage gives purpose to every scientific discovery, every clinical advance, and every connection we build.” 

The project is entering a new phase for both the construction team and the surrounding community. With site preparation, groundwater removal, excavation, and deep foundation work complete, Huntsman Cancer Institute in Vineyard is beginning to move above ground—turning months of complex construction into visible progress toward a future destination for cancer care, research, education, and discovery in Utah County. 

When complete, the 284,000-square-foot campus will expand Huntsman Cancer Institute's ability to serve the state and region through comprehensive cancer care, research, education, and training in Utah County. The cornerstone celebration offered a symbolic moment of permanence, honoring the supporters who helped build the foundation for the campus and the patients and families it will serve for generations. 

The cornerstone celebration reflected the broad coalition helping bring Huntsman Cancer Institute in Vineyard to life: patients, donors, public officials, community partners, educators, researchers, clinicians, scientists, staff, and residents who share a commitment to expanding access to cancer care and discovery. Speakers spoke about the power of partnership among community leaders, government officials, educational institutions, health care organizations, and philanthropic supporters to create lasting benefits for future generations. 

"Huntsman Cancer Institute in Vineyard is about much more than a new building. It’s a deliberate commitment to grow with Utah County."

Huntsman Cancer Institute's growth has long been driven by the generosity of donors, community advocates, and partners who share a commitment to reducing the burden of cancer. 

Michael Delzotti, FAHP, CFRE, president and chief operating officer of Huntsman Cancer Foundation, emphasized the significance of reaching a milestone community members can now see and experience. 

"Today, we celebrate the next step in the construction of Huntsman Cancer Institute in Vineyard," says Delzotti. "More than just a building, the Vineyard location embodies hope, bringing comprehensive care closer to patients and accelerating groundbreaking research that will bring us closer to a world without cancer. This essential work would not be possible without the generous support of philanthropic donors and other partners who are invested in improving care and ultimately ending cancer once and for all."

Image: Smiling Man Portrait With Purple Background

“We are so excited that this incredible facility will increase access to world-class health care for residents of Utah County and beyond. 
For Huntsman Cancer Institute leaders, the cornerstone celebration served as both a celebration and a reminder of the work that made this moment possible. Construction of the building's exterior structure will begin in fall 2026. By summer 2027, the building is expected to be fully enclosed, allowing interior construction and systems installation to move forward. The facility is anticipated to receive its certificate of occupancy in June 2028, with the first patients expected to be welcomed in September 2028. 

Utah legislative leaders commented on the important occasion. 

“This is a powerful example of what we can accomplish when Utahns come together,” Mike Schultz, Speaker of the Utah House of Representatives says. “By bringing world-class cancer care, research, and innovation closer to Utah families, we are investing not only in better health today, but in a stronger, healthier future for generations to come. I’m grateful to the Huntsman family, the University of Utah, our community partners, and everyone who has worked together to make this vision a reality.” 
“Huntsman Cancer Institute in Vineyard represents the best of Utah: innovation, collaboration, and a commitment to improving the lives of Utahns,” Utah Senate President J. Stuart Adams says. “By expanding access to world-class cancer care and creating new opportunities for research, education, and innovation, this campus will give more Utah families hope when they need it most. It will strengthen our communities, advance groundbreaking discoveries, and help ensure Utah continues to lead in developing treatments and cures that improve lives for generations to come.”

# Intermountain Health expands cancer services in St. George, bringing more specialized care closer to home

## Intermountain Health St. George Regional Hospital celebrated the expansion of its Cancer Center multidisciplinary clinic, marking a significant investment in cancer care for patients across Southern Utah and surrounding communities.

By 

Intermountain Health

//Sept 17, 2026

ST. GEORGE, Utah — Intermountain Health St. George Regional Hospital celebrated the expansion of its Cancer Center multidisciplinary clinic, marking a significant investment in cancer care for patients across Southern Utah and surrounding communities.

The expansion strengthens access to cancer specialists and supportive care services, helping more patients receive comprehensive care closer to home. The new space will allow Intermountain Health to expand palliative care services and create dedicated treatment space for infusions and other supportive care needs.

The additional capacity also creates opportunities to establish an advanced practice provider-led supportive care and survivorship clinic, giving patients access to resources that help manage symptoms, navigate treatment, and improve quality of life during and after cancer care.

# Intermountain Health Opens New Specialty Clinic and Cancer Center in Saratoga Springs to Meet Growing Community Needs

Saratoga Springs Ribbon Cutting

Intermountain Health is expanding access to specialized care close to home with the opening of the new Saratoga Springs Specialty Clinic and Cancer Center.

Intermountain Health built the new 48,000-square-foot facility on its existing campus, which also includes emergency services and a surgery center. This expansion creates a connected campus, allowing patients to receive more of their care in one convenient location.

The clinic opens Monday, Oct. 12, and will serve Saratoga Springs, Eagle Mountain, west Lehi, and other nearby communities.

“We’re proud to bring this level of coordinated care closer to the families we serve,” said Jason Wilson, president of Intermountain Health American Fork Hospital. “This is one of Utah’s fastest-growing areas, and we will help ensure people here have the medical care they need.”

The Fairbourne Campus represents a significant expansion of healthcare access in one of Utah’s fastest-growing communities.

Several services are expected to begin opening in early 2027, including medical oncology, infusion care, primary care sports medicine, neurology and cardiac rehabilitation. Additional planned services include advanced imaging, laboratory and pharmacy support, ambulatory and surgical care, endoscopy, orthopedics, rheumatology, rehabilitation and specialty physician clinics.

The first floor is planned to include imaging services and a future freestanding emergency department affiliated with Intermountain LDS Hospital. That emergency department is expected to open later in 2027.

The campus will complement—not replace—Intermountain’s existing West Valley Clinic, which will continue providing services such as primary care, family medicine, pediatrics and urgent care.

### Why It Matters

For many West Valley City residents, accessing specialty or hospital outpatient care currently means traveling to another part of the Salt Lake Valley. That extra distance can create real barriers for patients balancing work, transportation, childcare and ongoing treatment.

Bringing oncology, infusion, imaging, rehabilitation and other services closer to home can reduce travel time, make appointments easier to keep and help patients receive more coordinated care in one location.

The project also creates room to grow. With several floors available for future development, Intermountain can expand the campus over time based on the community’s evolving healthcare needs.

### The Bottom Line

The Fairbourne Campus represents a significant expansion of healthcare access in one of Utah’s fastest-growing communities. By converting an existing, centrally located building into a comprehensive medical hub, Intermountain Health aims to make high-quality care more convenient for West Valley City and west Salt Lake County residents for years to come.

Mar 01, 2025

At a celebratory groundbreaking in April 2025, work will advance on an endeavor that has been years in the making.

In 2024, Huntsman Cancer Institute marked 25 years since opening the first facility in Salt Lake City. Five major expansions followed, two mobile screening clinics launched, Huntsman at Home™ extended to rural Utah, and affiliate hospitals in five neighboring states worked to bring world-class cancer research, prevention, and care closer to where people live.

Today, Huntsman Cancer Institute is widely recognized as a world leader in eliminating distance as a cancer disparity. Bringing a Comprehensive Cancer Center to Vineyard is a key part of this work.

Years ago, leaders at Huntsman Cancer Institute reflected on the rapid population growth in Utah and the Mountain West, knowing we could not adequately meet the needs of the community from a single location.
